text: Every business that you have heard of has gotten rejected by at least a handful of venture capitalists at one point or another. And so that drive to keep going if you believe in the business is critical, absolutely critical.
speaker: Keith Yandell
context: Lenny asks Keith about advice for founders going through tough fundraising periods. Keith reflects on DoorDash's difficult Series D funding round, when they had very little runway left and had been rejected by numerous venture capitalists. He emphasizes that rejection is universal among successful businesses and shares how Tony Xu's persistence was crucial during their near-bankruptcy situation.
text_ko: 여러분이 들어본 거의 모든 사업은 언젠가 적어도 몇몇 벤처 투자자(venture capitalists)에게 거절당한 적이 있어요. 그러니까 비즈니스를 믿는다면 포기하지 않고 계속 나아가려는 의지가 정말 중요해요, 절대적으로 중요해요.
text_zh: 你听说过的每家公司，都在某个时候被好几位风险投资人(venture capitalists)拒过。所以如果你看好这门生意，能坚持下去的那股劲儿非常关键，真的至关重要。
text_es: Todas las empresas de las que has oído hablar han sido rechazadas por al menos un puñado de capitalistas de riesgo (venture capitalists) en algún momento. Por eso, el empuje para seguir adelante cuando crees en tu negocio es fundamental, absolutamente fundamental.
key_sentence: Every business faces rejection; the drive to keep going is critical.
original_text: Every business that you have heard of has gotten rejected by at least a handful of venture capitalists at one point or another. And so that drive to keep going if you believe in the business is critical, absolutely critical. I mean, we were weeks of runway situation and had been told no by everyone. And it was just Tony's drive, really, to keep going.

vocabulary.definition: Of great importance; essential for success or failure.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being 'critical' often refers to decisions or factors that can significantly impact the viability of a project or company.
vocabulary.nuance: While it can imply urgency, 'critical' also suggests a level of importance that cannot be understated, making it suitable for high-stakes discussions.

vocabulary.definition: Investors who provide capital to startups and small businesses with perceived long-term growth potential in exchange for equity.
vocabulary.businessContext: Venture capitalists play a crucial role in the startup ecosystem by funding innovative ideas and helping entrepreneurs scale their businesses.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of high risk and high reward, as venture capitalists typically invest in early-stage companies that may not yet be profitable.

text: And for me, one of the top things I always hear about DoorDash from an executive standpoint when we do the internal survey is it's a "no politics, no asshole" culture.
speaker: Keith Yandell
context: Lenny asks Keith about a story where he called a candidate an "asshole" during the interview process. Keith explains DoorDash's "no politics, no asshole" culture and describes how Ryan Sokol, who is now their VP of engineering, initially came across as aloof and gave curt answers during his interview, which made Keith concerned about cultural fit.
text_ko: 제 경험상, 내부 설문조사를 하면 임원들 사이에서 도어대시(DoorDash)에 대해 가장 자주 듣는 말 중 하나가 "정치질 없고 무례한 사람이 없는 문화"예요.
text_zh: 对我来说，我们做内部调查时，高管们常说DoorDash有种“不搞办公室政治、不容混蛋”的文化（'no politics, no asshole'）。
text_es: Para mí, una de las principales cosas que siempre oigo sobre DoorDash por parte de los ejecutivos, cuando hacemos la encuesta interna, es que tienen una cultura de "sin juegos de poder ni gente tóxica" (no politics, no asshole).
key_sentence: DoorDash has a no politics, no asshole culture from an executive standpoint.
original_text: And for me, one of the top things I always hear about DoorDash from an executive standpoint when we do the internal survey is it's a "no politics, no asshole" culture. And I'm not one to swear a lot, but after interviewing Ryan Sokol, who's now our VP of eng, he was just kind of aloof. He came off as aloof to me, really curt answers.

vocabulary.definition: A perspective or viewpoint that reflects the considerations and priorities of senior management or executives within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, discussing issues from an executive standpoint often involves focusing on strategic decisions, financial implications, and overall organizational goals.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the importance of high-level decision-making and may imply a disconnect from the operational or employee-level perspectives.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic method of gathering information and feedback from employees within an organization to assess various aspects of the workplace.
vocabulary.businessContext: Internal surveys are commonly used in businesses to gauge employee satisfaction, engagement, and organizational culture, often influencing management decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: While valuable for insight, internal surveys may be subject to bias if employees feel their responses could impact their job security.

vocabulary.definition: The shared values, beliefs, and behaviors that characterize an organization and influence its practices and interactions among employees.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, culture plays a critical role in shaping employee engagement, retention, and overall organizational effectiveness, often being a key factor in recruitment.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry both positive and negative connotations, depending on whether it reflects a supportive environment or a toxic atmosphere.

vocabulary.definition: The activities, actions, or policies used to gain and maintain power within an organization, often involving negotiation and influence among individuals or groups.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, politics can refer to the dynamics of power relationships that affect decision-making and resource allocation, sometimes leading to conflicts or alliances.
vocabulary.nuance: While some level of politics is inevitable in organizations, excessive political maneuvering can create a toxic work environment and hinder collaboration.

text: Life's too short to work with people you don't really enjoy.
speaker: Keith Yandell
context: Keith continues the story about Ryan Sokol's hiring process. After having dinner and addressing the cultural concerns directly, Ryan later explained that DoorDash's willingness to potentially reject a qualified candidate solely based on attitude actually convinced him to join. This demonstrated to Ryan that the company genuinely prioritized cultural fit over just technical qualifications.
text_ko: 인생은 짧아요. 함께 일하는 게 정말 즐겁지 않은 사람들과는 굳이 일하지 않는 게 좋아요.
text_zh: 人生苦短，别跟合不来的人共事。
text_es: La vida es demasiado corta para trabajar con gente con la que no disfrutas colaborar.
key_sentence: Life's too short to work with people you don't really enjoy.
original_text: And six months later, he told me that one of the reasons why he joined DoorDash was that we were going to blackball him potentially from joining just because of his attitude, because his perspective is life's too short to work with people you don't really enjoy, and a lot of people pay lip service.

vocabulary.definition: To take pleasure in or derive satisfaction from an experience or activity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a workplace setting, enjoying one's work can lead to higher morale, productivity, and employee retention, making it a critical factor in organizational culture.
vocabulary.nuance: While the term is generally positive, it should be used carefully in professional contexts to maintain a balance between enjoyment and professionalism.

text: If you want to achieve a 10x outcome, hiring someone that's an expert in the field, it's maybe unlikely you're going to achieve that 10x outcome, because they're likely to do things the way things have always been done.
speaker: Keith Yandell
context: Lenny asks Keith how he's able to credibly lead teams in areas where he lacks expertise. Keith explains Tony Xu's philosophy from the book "Range" about why generalists can be better than specialists. He describes how Tony deliberately puts people in roles outside their expertise area because domain experts tend to stick to conventional approaches, while outsiders are more likely to completely reimagine systems and achieve breakthrough results.
text_ko: 만약 10배 성과(10x outcome)를 내고 싶다면, 해당 분야의 전문가를 채용한다고 해서 그 목표를 달성할 가능성은 낮아요. 전문가들은 대개 기존에 해오던 방식대로 일을 처리하려는 경향이 있거든요.
text_zh: 如果你想实现10倍的成果 (10x outcome)，去请行业里的专家反而不太可能做到，因为他们往往会照老一套做事。
text_es: Si buscas un resultado 10x (10x outcome), es poco probable que lo consigas contratando a alguien que sea experto en el sector; lo más normal es que haga las cosas como siempre se han hecho.
key_sentence: they're likely to do things the way things have always been done.
original_text: If you want to achieve a 10x outcome, hiring someone that's an expert in the field, it's maybe unlikely you're going to achieve that 10x outcome, because they're likely to do things the way things have always been done. So you might achieve incremental benefits, but the odds of completely reinventing the system and doing something that's vastly superior to others is much lower.

vocabulary.definition: To successfully reach a desired objective or result through effort or skill.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'achieve' often refers to meeting specific goals, such as sales targets, project milestones, or performance metrics.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, suggesting accomplishment and success, and is often used in motivational contexts.

vocabulary.definition: A person with extensive knowledge or skill in a particular area or field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, hiring an expert is often seen as a strategy to gain insights and improve performance in specialized areas.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'expert' implies a high level of competence, it can also suggest rigidity in thinking, as experts may adhere closely to established practices.

text: And I think it's a big part of our success, is this desire to be successful, regardless of who's in charge. And that comes from the fact when I joined DoorDash, we were getting our tails kicked. We were in fourth place in the space.
speaker: Keith Yandell
context: Keith discusses his philosophy of hiring people better than himself and then getting out of their way as they succeed. He explains how this collaborative mindset became part of DoorDash's DNA because when he joined, the company was struggling badly - they were in fourth place in food delivery and Uber had just entered the market and quickly gained leadership position.
text_ko: 그리고 저는 누가 책임자든 상관없이 성공하려는 그 마음가짐이 우리 성공의 큰 부분이라고 생각해요. 그건 제가 DoorDash에 합류했을 때 우리가 엄청 고전하고 있었던 경험에서 온 거예요. 그때 우리는 그 분야에서 4위였어요.
text_zh: 我觉得这是我们成功的一个重要原因：大家都有那股想成功的劲儿，不管谁当家。因为我加入 DoorDash 的时候，我们当时被打得很惨，在这条赛道上只排第四。
text_es: Y creo que gran parte de nuestro éxito se debe a ese deseo de triunfar, sin importar quién esté a cargo. Y eso viene de que cuando me uní a DoorDash nos estaban ganando por goleada; estábamos en cuarto lugar en ese mercado.
key_sentence: Our success stems from the desire to succeed despite getting our tails kicked.
original_text: And I think it's a big part of our success, is this desire to be successful, regardless of who's in charge. And that comes from the fact when I joined DoorDash, we were getting our tails kicked. We were in fourth place in the space. Uber had just launched food and rocket to market share leadership.

vocabulary.definition: Success is the achievement of a desired aim, goal, or purpose, often measured by the attainment of financial, operational, or personal milestones.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, success can be quantified through metrics such as revenue growth, market share, and customer satisfaction, and is a primary objective for organizations.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'success' generally connotes positive outcomes, it can also imply pressure to maintain or exceed previous achievements, making it a complex and sometimes subjective term.

vocabulary.definition: Regardless means without paying attention to the present situation; it indicates a lack of concern for certain factors or conditions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'regardless' is often used to emphasize commitment to goals or actions despite challenges or changes in leadership or circumstances.
vocabulary.nuance: This term can carry a tone of determination, but it may also suggest a disregard for important details, so it should be used carefully to avoid appearing dismissive.

text: And so one thing I noticed is, it's hard to come into a place and be new and understand how things work and what it means to be successful there. And so the idea was to do our best to scale that.
speaker: Keith Yandell
context: Lenny asks Keith about his "How to work with Keith" document that he created for his teams. Keith explains that as DoorDash was growing rapidly (2-3x headcount each year), it became difficult to scale culture and help new employees understand how to be successful. Tony Xu taught him that written documentation is one of the most effective ways to scale knowledge and culture across a fast-growing organization.
text_ko: 제가 하나 느낀 건, 새로운 곳에 들어가 신입으로서 그 조직이 어떻게 돌아가는지, 거기서 성공하려면 무엇이 필요한지 이해하기가 참 어렵다는 점이에요. 그래서 그걸 최대한 확장(scale)할 수 있도록 최선을 다하자는 생각이었어요.
text_zh: 我发现一件事：刚到一个地方当新人的时候，很难弄清楚这里怎么运作、什么才算是成功。我们的想法就是尽力把这些做法规模化（scale），让更多人能更快上手。
text_es: Me di cuenta de que es difícil llegar a un sitio siendo nuevo y entender cómo funcionan las cosas y qué significa tener éxito allí. Por eso quisimos hacer todo lo posible para escalar eso (scale).
key_sentence: it's hard to come into a place and be new and understand how things work and what it means to be successful there.
original_text: And so one thing I noticed is, it's hard to come into a place and be new and understand how things work and what it means to be successful there. And so the idea was to do our best to scale that. And one thing that Tony taught me is one thing that scales really well is written work.

vocabulary.definition: To increase in size, amount, or capacity in a systematic way, often in relation to business operations or production.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, scaling refers to the ability of a company to grow and manage increased demand without compromising performance or losing revenue potential.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'scale' often implies growth, it can also suggest the need for efficiency and sustainability in operations.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something; to comprehend.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding is crucial for effective communication, decision-making, and strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a deeper level of insight beyond surface-level knowledge, often requiring analysis and experience.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving desired aims or attaining prosperity; marked by favorable outcomes or accomplishments.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, success is often measured by profitability, market share, and the achievement of strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry subjective meanings depending on individual or organizational goals, and what constitutes success can vary widely.

text: And so now if I get a blind reference, people are going to hear that, "It's not all about the company. It's not all about Keith. It's about you and your career," and that's going to pay back 10x.
speaker: Keith Yandell
context: Keith explains his philosophy of helping employees find their next job, even if it's outside DoorDash. He describes the long-term benefits of this approach - when people do reference checks on him as a manager, they hear that he puts employees' career interests first. This reputation pays dividends in attracting talent, even if it occasionally means losing someone who would have left eventually anyway.
text_ko: 그러면 이제 제가 블라인드 레퍼런스(blind reference)를 받으면 사람들은 "이건 회사 이야기만 하는 게 아니고, 키스(Keith) 이야기만 하는 것도 아니에요. 당신과 당신의 커리어(career)를 위한 거예요."라고 들을 거고, 그게 10배로 돌아올 거예요.
text_zh: 所以现在，如果有人给我做盲推荐（blind reference），别人会听到我说：“这不全是为了公司，也不全是为了Keith，而是为了你和你的职业发展”，这会带来十倍回报（10x）。
text_es: Así que ahora, si recibo una referencia a ciegas (blind reference), la gente va a escuchar: "No se trata solo de la empresa. No se trata solo de Keith. Se trata de ti y de tu carrera", y eso va a dar un retorno diez veces mayor.
key_sentence: A blind reference emphasizes it's about your career, paying back 10x.
original_text: And so now if I get a blind reference, people are going to hear that, "It's not all about the company. It's not all about Keith. It's about you and your career," and that's going to pay back 10x. Maybe you lose one really talented person, but they probably shouldn't be there anyway. They're probably going to leave anyway.

vocabulary.definition: To return money that was borrowed or to compensate someone for a favor or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'pay back' can refer to the return on investment (ROI) that a company expects from a project or initiative, indicating the financial benefits gained over time.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used in a financial context, 'pay back' can also imply a moral obligation to reciprocate support or assistance.
